title: How to organize the utensil and utility drawers | Kitchen
description:
The shallow drawers holding hand tools: flatware, spatulas, peelers, measuring spoons, foil and wraps.

This is the Utensil and Utility Drawers in the Kitchen. About 15-30 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Each drawer has one job and a name written inside its front edge. Flatware sits in a divided insert with nothing loose beside it. Foil, cling film, and baking paper stand on end so you can read the boxes from above. Every drawer closes flush with one push.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Tip one drawer at a time onto a tea towel and put back only what you have used since the season changed.
Straighten: Dividers go in before anything else, and you name the drawer before you fill it.
Shine: Lift the insert right out and tip the grit, because the crumbs that jam a drawer collect underneath the divide

Standardize: Write the name inside each drawer front: flatware, cooking tools, wraps and bags, utility.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
One category per drawer, named inside the front edge, blades sheathed, and every drawer closing with one push.
